ad15_lobbying.topic: Federal lobbying by industry, campaign finance, influence evidence, revolving door, Direct File case

claims.text: Statista: total lobbying spending $4.27bn in 2023 and $4.44bn in 2024
LegiStorm: $5.24bn in 2025, up $768m from 2024 (about 17%); outside firms $2.76bn (+25.3%), in-house $2.46bn (+8.5%); 15,592 clients vs 13,910

NBC/OpenSecrets: federal lobbying a record $4.2bn in 2023; health sector over $739m, the most of any sector; Chamber of Commerce $69m and NAR $52m in 2023; NAR $82m and Chamber $81m in 2022; state lobbying $1.4bn in 2023

OpenSecrets Q2 2025: pharmaceuticals and health products $105.4m in Q2, $226.8m in first half 2025; pharma outspent every industry in all but one quarter since 2010; real estate $34.1m; Chamber $19.8m, NAR $16.2m; AHIP $4.1m; the OBBBA was the most-lobbied bill (2,145 clients)

Citizens United, decided 21 January 2010: limits on corporate independent expenditures (2 U.S.C. 441b) invalid; Austin overruled and part of McConnell; disclaimer and disclosure upheld; independent expenditures 'do not give rise to corruption or the appearance of corruption'

Brennan Center (2025): 5-4 ruling; in 2024 more than $1bn from anonymous sources to committees supporting candidates of both parties; roughly 44% ($481m) of money raised to support Trump came from 10 donors; top 10 Harris donors nearly 8% ($126m); Musk at least $277m; Adelson over $100m

Gilens and Page (2014): 1,779 policy issues 1981-2002; average citizens have little or no independent influence; low elite support passes ~18%, high ~45%; business groups about twice the influence of mass-based groups

Bashir (2015): elite coefficient 0.76 vs median 0.03; income-group preferences correlated (r 0.78 corrected); R-squared 0.074; when median-income Americans favour change at 80%+ it happens 47% vs 52% for elites; in 185 disagreement cases median-income side wins 47%
Enns (2015): 50th and 90th percentile relative support correlated r=0.94 across 1,836 questions; 'Coincidental representation appears to be the norm'; strong partisans show larger gaps
Blanes i Vidal et al. (2012): ex-Senate staffer lobbyists see a 24% drop in generated revenue when their senator leaves office
HLOGA signed 14 Sept 2007 by George W. Bush (Senate 96-2, House 411-8): senators' cooling-off 1 to 2 years; quarterly LDA filings; bundling disclosure over $15,000

Bloomberg Tax: Intuit about $3m federal lobbying in first three quarters 2025 ($2.9m same period 2024); H&R Block $2.4m; ACTR (representing both) $270,000; July 2025 tax law gave IRS $15m to study a public-private alternative; provision to end Direct File removed; Intuit: 'regularly engages with policymakers'

AP: IRS email: 'IRS Direct File will not be available in Filing Season 2026'; accepted returns 140,803 (2024) and 296,531 (2025); Bessent: 'better alternatives', 'wasn't used very much'; average American spends about $140 a year preparing returns
Intuit FY2025 (to 31 July 2025): revenue $18.8bn; Consumer Group $4.9bn (+10%); TurboTax Live $2.0bn

ad15_financialization.topic: Finance share of profits; Krippner; forced arbitration and class-action waivers

claims.text: Krippner: financialization 'a pattern of accumulation in which profits accrue primarily through financial channels'; ratio of financial to non-financial profits at end of period roughly three to five times 1950s-60s level; nonfinancial firms' portfolio income ratio peaked late 1980s about five times earlier levels

Concepcion, 27 April 2011, 5-4 (Scalia; Breyer dissent): FAA preempts California's Discover Bank rule that held class-arbitration waivers unconscionable; dispute over sales tax on phones advertised as free
Epic Systems, 21 May 2018, 5-4 (Gorsuch; Ginsburg dissent): 'arbitration agreements providing for individualized proceedings must be enforced'; NLRA does not override

CFPB (10 July 2017): study found issuers with over half of card debt and banks with 44% of insured deposits used arbitration clauses; 3 in 4 consumers did not know; about 2% would consider legal action over small dispute; group lawsuits paid 34m+ consumers $1bn over five years; in about 1,000 arbitrations over two years arbitrators awarded about $360,000 to 78 consumers; Congress disapproved under the CRA, signed 1 Nov 2017; removed from CFR 22 Nov 2017
House voted 231-190 (July 2017); Senate 51-50 on 24 Oct 2017 with Vice President Pence breaking the tie; Chamber of Commerce sued 29 Sept 2017

Treasury (23 Oct 2017) critique: by the Bureau's own projections four in five class actions yield no recovery for class members; on average 4% of class members claim; typical payment $32.35; about $330m more to plaintiffs' counsel over five years

Colvin/EPI (2018): employer survey 2017; 56.2% of nonunion private-sector employees (about 60.1 million) under mandatory arbitration vs about 2% in 1992; 41.1% of covered employees (23.1% of all, 24.7m) face class-action waivers; 64.5% of establishments with average wage under $13/hour
Ending Forced Arbitration of Sexual Assault and Sexual Harassment Act: sponsors Gillibrand (D) and Graham (R); Senate voice vote; signed 3 March 2022; claimant chooses court or arbitration

ad15_pricing.topic: Markups, concentration critics, surveillance pricing, junk fees, right to repair

claims.text: De Loecker, Eeckhout and Unger (QJE 2020): average markups rose from 21% above marginal cost in 1980 to 61% 'now'; profit rate 1% to 8%; driven by upper tail, median unchanged; mostly within industries

Basu (2019): 'Existing methods cannot determine whether markups have been stable or whether they have risen modestly'; methods rest on cost minimisation; some steep-rise results hard to reconcile with aggregate data

FTC staff 17 Jan 2025: initial findings of the July 2024 6(b) study of eight intermediaries (unanimous orders): demographics, location, browsing and inferred data can be used to set individual prices; RFI docket FTC-2025-0007; Ferguson and Holyoak dissented from releasing preliminary findings and said a final fact-based report would follow

Instacart ended retailer price experiments 22 Dec 2025 after a CR/Groundwork/More Perfect Union investigation found different prices for the same items at the same time; Instacart said software did not meaningfully raise prices; FTC reportedly opened an investigation (Reuters 17 Dec); separate $60m Instacart+ refund settlement 18 Dec 2025

New York Algorithmic Pricing Disclosure Act (signed May 2025, effective 8 July 2025) requires a conspicuous disclosure next to prices set by algorithm using personal data, fines up to $1,000; Judge Rakoff dismissed NRF First Amendment suit (Oct 2025)
FTC Rule on Unfair or Deceptive Fees finalised Dec 2024, effective 12 May 2025, covers live-event tickets and short-term lodging

Consumer electronics right-to-repair laws: New York (effective 28 Dec 2023), California and Minnesota (1 July 2024), Colorado (1 Jan 2026), Oregon; parts, tools and documentation on fair and reasonable terms; Oregon and Colorado restrict parts pairing
FTC 'Nixing the Fix' (May 2021, unanimous, mandated by Congress) found 'scant evidence to support manufacturers' justifications for repair restrictions'

Apple battery throttling settlement: up to $500m, at least $25 per iPhone (SE, 6, 6s, 7 models on iOS 10.2.1 and later); throttling undisclosed until Dec 2017; preliminary approval May 2020; no admission of wrongdoing

claims.text: Breyer dissent in Concepcion: 'What rational lawyer would have signed on to represent the Concepcions in litigation for the possibility of fees stemming from a $30.22 claim?'

Italian Colors, 20 June 2013, 5-3 (Scalia; Kagan dissent joined by Ginsburg and Breyer; Sotomayor not participating): class-arbitration waiver enforced although expert proof would cost 'at least several hundred thousand dollars, and might exceed $1 million' against a maximum individual recovery of $12,850 ($38,549 trebled); Kagan: 'Too darn bad'

CFPB (10 July 2017): Congress already prohibits arbitration agreements in the residential mortgage market and has prohibited them in many forms of credit extended to servicemembers (Military Lending Act)
